sentences.text: Researchers used a viral vector to increase the protein TFEB specifically in excitatory neurons of the hippocampus in young mice carrying a genetic model of Alzheimer's disease.

This targeted boost lowered the amount of a toxic protein in the brain, reduced the number of protein clumps and damaged nerve endings, and improved the mice's ability to learn and remember locations.
The intervention sped up the brain cells' waste-removal system and also improved the function of the cells' energy-producing structures.

In a lab-grown cell line that produces the Alzheimer's protein, adding TFEB increased markers of the waste-removal system, boosted energy production, and lowered the amount of protein inside the cells.
The authors conclude that activating this specific protein in brain cells early in the disease process helps clear toxic waste and protects against further brain damage.
